To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
amitraz hydrolysis depends on the pH, temperature, ionic strength of the medium, solvent composition, and surfactant concentration.
amitraz hydrolysis was fastest in water and slower in organic solvent mixtures and in surfactant solutions.
amitraz hydrolyzes by a pseudo-first-order process and that the hydrolysis depends on the pH of the solution, the temperature of the solution, and the presence of solvents and surfactants.

developing an understanding of the factors that influence the hydrolysis and degradation of amitraz, a widely used veterinary drug.

hydrolysis of Amitraz is a complex process and that the hydrolysis is influenced by a number of factors.
the rate of hydrolysis of the amitraz molecule depends on the solvent and the surfactant present.
amitraz hydrolysis is influenced by the solution pH, ionic strength and buffer capacity, solvent dielectric constant, and the presence of surfactants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hydrolysis rates of amitraz are affected by solution properties and can be enhanced by the use of organic solvents and surfactants.
amitraz hydrolysis is a pH dependent, first order, pseudo first order, and a type ABC pH rate profile.
the rate of hydrolysis of the drug is affected by solution properties such as buffer concentration, ionic strength and pH and by solvent and surfactant composition.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the rate of hydrolysis of the pesticide amitraz depends on the dielectric properties of solvent mixtures, the ionic strength and composition of the buffer, the pH, the presence of surfactants, and temperature.
amitraz can be solubilized and degraded using surfactants and that the rate of hydrolysis can be manipulated by varying the pH and temperature.
the degradation of amitraz can be controlled by changing the solution conditions and that this knowledge can be used in the development of effective disposal strategies for this drug.
